Структура слога не изучена. 5.1.2. Типы чередований не изучены. [p. 816] О т р и ц а н и е во всех видо-временних формах, кроме императива, осуществляется с помощью частицы na ‛неʼ: ná ku lekʰem ‛не вижуʼ, na lekʰecʰir ‛ты не увиделʼ, na eir lekʰer ‛ты не виделʼ, na lekʰes piti ‛ты не увидишьʼ. В императиве используется запретительная частица má ‛неʼ: ma lekʰe ‛не смотриʼ, ma lekʰekʰ ‛не смотритеʼ. Обе частицы являются «исконными» грамматическими элементами. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (as in the Western Armenian grammatical matrix of the language); examples are bare citation forms.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated explicitly. The sketch adds that syllable structure and alternations are 'not studied' (5.1.1-5.1.2). On p. 816 the negative particle na and prohibitive ma are printed with an acute in examples (ná ku lekʰem 'I do not see', má), suggesting these proclitic particles attract stress as in Armenian, but no rule is formulated; behaviour of the enclitic definite article -ə/-n is not discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('последний слог слова'), illustrated with isolated citation forms; the sketch describes the Armenia/Georgia dialect of Lomavren (sec. 2.0), whose speakers are L1 Armenian and use Lomavren as a secret register.
new_statements.identity_note: Voskanian 2011 explicitly describes the Lomavren variety of Armenia and southern Georgia (Yerevan, Gyumri, Akhalkalaki, Akhaltsikhe), not the Turkish (Kars/Artvin) variety; this is the variety Glottolog Lomavren is an Armenian-grammar mixed language/secret register whose speakers are L1 (Western-type) Armenian speakers; the final-stress rule matches the Armenian matrix.

sources.note: p. 812 (sec. 5.1.0): dynamic stress, falls on the last syllable of the word, with examples manús, mančʰáv, čahrí, čʰətár, buhú. Negation/prohibitive particles are written with an acute (ná ku lekʰem, má) on p. 816 but no rule is stated for them.
Nothing on phonology or stress; references only Ethnologue, Encyclopaedia Iranica 'Gypsy ii', LINGUIST List.
